terms.gloss: the base: the pastry case or the base of a cake, pie, or tart
evidence: Cato Agr. 76: inde facitō solum tenue
Cato Agr. 76: posteā solum contrahitō ōrnātōque
terms.comment: In Cato’s cakes the solum is the sheet of dough laid under the filling, whose edge is then drawn up round it (solum contrahere), as a pastry case is made; the word is the ordinary one for the bottom of anything.

phrases.latin: Massam extende et solum in fōrmā fac.
phrases.english: Roll out the dough and make the pastry case in the tin.

phrases.latin: Solum ex crustulīs contūsīs et būtȳrō faciēmus.
phrases.english: We’ll make the base out of crushed biscuits and butter.

phrases.latin: posteā farīnae L. II cōnspargitō condepsitōque. inde facitō solum tenue
phrases.english: then sprinkle two pounds of flour with water and knead it; then make a thin base

phrases.latin: in summum tracta singula inditō, posteā solum contrahitō ōrnātōque
phrases.english: put single sheets of pastry on top, then draw up the base and finish it neatly

sources: Lewis & Short: solum
